title: Lecture introduction and learning aims
groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's place in the course and introduces its intended learning outcomes.

title: Molecular changes driving clonal evolution and tumor development
groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how changes in gene function or activity confer properties that enable cells to expand and develop into tumors.

title: Stemness, tumor hierarchy and the cell of origin
groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell's position in a differentiation hierarchy affects its capacity to initiate and propagate cancer.

title: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer promotion
groupedBecause: These subtopics show how inflammatory signaling can give mutation-bearing cells the stem-like properties needed for tumor formation.

title: Stromal dependence of established tumors and therapeutic targeting
groupedBecause: This subtopic examines established tumors' dependence on supportive stromal cells as a vulnerability that treatment could exploit.

title: Investigating cancer evolution with single-cell and spatial omics
groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tissue-based molecular methods reveal tumor evolution and interactions between cells.

title: Converging conditions for malignant outgrowth
groupedBecause: This synthesis explains cancer development as the convergence of cellular fitness and a permissive environment at the right time and place.

title: Lecture close and next lecture
groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces the forthcoming session on therapy.
